name: Food trivia (medium)
description: 28 medium questions about dishes, ingredients, cuisines, cooking terms. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which three vegetables make up the classic French flavor base called mirepoix?
items.explain: Mirepoix is a combination of onions, carrots and celery, used as a base for stocks, soups, stews and sauces.

items.question: In Cajun and Louisiana Creole cooking, the "holy trinity" uses bell pepper in place of which vegetable from French mirepoix?
items.explain: The Cajun trinity is onions, bell peppers and celery. The carrots of traditional mirepoix were swapped for bell peppers, partly because of availability and cost.

items.question: Which part of the Crocus sativus flower is dried to make the spice saffron?
items.explain: Saffron is made from the dried, golden-colored stigmas of the autumn crocus. Each flower has three of them.

items.question: Which compound gives saffron its rich golden color?
items.explain: Saffron contains a dye called crocin that gives food a rich golden color. Curcumin is the pigment in turmeric.

items.question: Which rice variety do most paella cooks use?
items.explain: Most paella cooks use bomba rice. A cultivar called senia is also used in the Valencia region.

items.question: In Spain, on which day of the week is paella traditionally included on restaurant menus?
items.explain: In Spain, paella is traditionally included on restaurant menus on Thursdays.

items.question: What happens to a roux's thickening power as it is cooked to a darker color?
answers: It increases as the flavor deepens
It decreases as the flavor deepens
It stays the same at every color
It increases as the flavor fades
items.correct: It decreases as the flavor deepens
items.explain: The darker a roux gets, the less thickening power it has. A chocolate roux has about one-fourth the thickening power of a white roux by weight.

items.question: A classic roux is made from what ratio of fat to flour by weight?
items.explain: Roux is typically made from equal parts of flour and fat by weight, cooked together to thicken sauces.

items.question: Which of these classic French sauces is NOT made with a roux?
items.explain: Roux is used in béchamel, velouté and espagnole. Hollandaise is thickened by emulsifying egg yolks and butter instead.

items.question: Which royal chef established the original four French mother sauces a century before Auguste Escoffier revised the list?
items.explain: Carême enshrined the original four sauces (velouté, béchamel, allemande and espagnole). Escoffier later added hollandaise and tomato and reclassified allemande.

source.title: The Mothers of All French Sauces

items.question: Béarnaise sauce, flavored with tarragon, shallot and white wine vinegar, is a derivative of which mother sauce?
items.explain: Béarnaise is made from hollandaise with tarragon, shallot and white wine vinegar added.

source.title: What Are the 5 Mother Sauces? And Their Derivatives

items.question: Which French mother sauce is made by adding milk to a white roux?
items.explain: Béchamel is built on a blonde white roux with milk added. Velouté and the other mother sauces use stock.

items.question: The browning reaction between amino acids and sugars that flavors seared meat and toast is named after which French chemist?
items.explain: The Maillard reaction is named after the French chemist Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in the early 1900s.

source.title: Maillard reactions change the tastes of your food

items.question: Which ingredient, now standard in kimchi, was unknown in Korea until the early seventeenth century?
items.explain: Chili peppers are a New World crop and were unknown in Korea until the early 1600s. Earlier kimchi was not spicy red.

items.question: Kimchi was traditionally fermented and buried in the ground in ceramic pots known by what Korean name?
items.explain: In Korea, kimchi was fermented in traditional brown ceramic pots called onggi, often buried in the ground in winter.

items.question: Gazpacho, a cold soup of raw blended vegetables, is most closely associated with which region of Spain?
items.explain: Gazpacho, also called Andalusian gazpacho, is a cold soup from Andalusia in southern Spain.

items.question: Despite its name, what is gazpacho manchego?
items.explain: Gazpacho manchego is a meat stew served hot, not a variation on the cold vegetable soup.

items.question: Which nut forms the base of ajoblanco, the Andalusian "white gazpacho"?
items.explain: Ajoblanco is a cold soup of bread, almonds, garlic, water and olive oil, sometimes called white gazpacho.

items.question: Guanciale, the cured meat traditionally used in Roman carbonara, comes from which part of the pig?
items.explain: Guanciale is an Italian salt-cured meat made from pork jowl or cheeks. Its rendered fat flavors and thickens pasta sauces.

items.question: Most Italian sources trace the origin of pasta carbonara to which region?
items.explain: Most Italian sources place carbonara's origin in Lazio, the region around Rome.

items.question: What is the minimum aging period for Parmigiano-Reggiano?
items.explain: Parmigiano-Reggiano is a raw cow's milk PDO cheese aged at least 12 months. Most of it is sold at 24 to 36 months.

source.title: Parmigiano-Reggiano: How to Spot the Real DOP Wheel

items.question: Which herb is added during the production of Cypriot halloumi, giving it a slight minty flavor?
items.explain: Halloumi has a slight minty flavor because spearmint is added during production.

items.question: What does the French cooking term "sous vide" literally mean?
items.explain: Sous vide means "under vacuum." Food is vacuum-sealed and then slowly cooked in water at a low, controlled temperature.

items.question: From which seaweed did Kikunae Ikeda isolate glutamate in 1908, leading him to name the taste umami?
items.explain: In 1908 Ikeda identified glutamate, found in large quantities in kombu seaweed, as the source of the savory taste he called umami.

items.question: What plant is widely used in place of real wasabi in the paste served outside Japan?
items.explain: Real wasabi is costly and hard to cultivate. Western horseradish is widely used in its place.

items.question: Which genus of mold binds cooked soybeans together into a firm cake of tempeh?
items.explain: Tempeh consists of cooked and fermented soybeans bound together by the mycelium of Rhizopus oligosporus.

items.question: Tempeh, a fermented whole-soybean cake, originated in which country?
items.explain: Tempeh is a fermented soy food that originated in Indonesia, where it is still the most popular soy food.

items.question: Which flavor base of garlic, onion and peppers cooked in olive oil is common in Spanish and Latin American cooking?
items.explain: Sofrito is a base of garlic, onion and peppers cooked in olive oil, sometimes with tomatoes or carrots.
